text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romanian Oil Company CRP will not require new fuel prices hikes yet, said Vifor Ionita CRP general manager.
- Romania's economy is in difficulty and reforms must be quickly impemented, said Kenneth Lay, head of the World Bank team visiting Bucharest this week.
- Romanias' central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said that the National Bank started to soack money supply in excess, with toughened policy and higher interest rates.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian Oil Company has $100 million in overdue debts, said company president Mihail Georgescu.
- In 30 years from now Romania will exhaust crude reserves, newspaper quotes Petrom oil company sources as saying.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The government has postponed price rises for another three weeks in order to get the money for social protection, newspaper quotes Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea as saying.
ZIUA
- Parlamentary budget, finance and banking commission will quizz central bank governor Mugur Isarescu.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- The central bank will not resort to adminstrative intervention to bridge the gap between interbank and retail currency rates, a central bank official said.
LIBERTATEA
- Minimum monthly wage should be set at 200,000 lei, union leader Bogdan Hossu said.
- Tensions sparked by a row between the manager and the main shareholder of private Romanian BANKCOOP SA bank have been defused.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian border police hauled 5,000 kilos of drugs last year, police Colonel Constantin Buzoianu said.
- U.S. Bell Helicopter will donate $25,000 to orphanages in Brasov County, where the U.S. company took over a local helicopter maker in a $1.0 billion project signed last year.
ADEVARUL
- Jiu Valley coal miners plan rally in their western mining centre of Petrosani on Saturday, protesting over the recent detention of their boss, Miron Cosma, for his role in post-communist riots.
- Editorial on the "need for change" in ex-President Ion Iliescu's leftwing Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), which starts conference to elect leaders after it lost elections in November 1996.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Editorial on the significance of the PDSR conference following party's ouster from power during elections last November.
CRONICA ROMANA
- "A modern party should always adjust to new realities," ex-President Ion Iliescu says in interview ahead of his former ruling party's conference on Friday.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Ex-President Ion Iliescu will return as head of the Party of Social Democracy (PDSR), paper quotes PDSR spokesman as saying ahead of the party's conference on Friday.
LIBERTATEA

- White-collar crime is on the rise in Romania, newspaper says, quoting police chief as saying that Romania is the "only country in Europe without laws against money laundering and fraudulent pyramid investment schemes".
COTIDIANUL
- Defence Minister Victor Babiuc told reporters at his first news conference that Romania must do its best to join NATO in a first wave of admissions. -- Bucharest Newsroom, 40-1 3120264 REUTER
